Introduction to Neural Networks

A Neural Network is a series of algorithms that are modeled after the human brain. It is designed to recognize patterns in data and make predictions based on those patterns. Neural Networks consist of layers of interconnected nodes, or neurons, which process information and send signals to other neurons. The output of one layer becomes the input to the next layer, allowing the network to learn and improve its predictions.

Weights and Bias

In a Neural Network, each connection between two neurons has a weight associated with it. These weights determine the strength of the connection between the neurons. During the training process, the network adjusts the weights to optimize the performance of the model. Additionally, each neuron has a bias, which is a constant value added to the weighted sum of the inputs to the neuron. This bias helps to adjust the output of the neuron.

Different Types of Layers

There are several types of layers that can be used in a Neural Network. The most common types are:

  • Input Layer: This layer receives the input data and passes it on to the next layer.
  • Hidden Layers: These layers perform computations on the input data and pass the results to the next layer. There can be multiple hidden layers in a Neural Network.
  • Output Layer: This layer produces the output of the Neural Network.

Activation Function

An activation function is used to introduce non-linearity into the Neural Network. This non-linearity allows the network to learn complex patterns in the data. There are several activation functions available, such as:

  • ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit)
  • Sigmoid
  • Tanh (Hyperbolic Tangent)
  • Softmax

Gradient Descent and Stochastic Gradient Descent

Gradient Descent is an optimization algorithm used to minimize the loss function of the Neural Network. It works by iteratively adjusting the weights and biases to find the minimum value of the loss function. Stochastic Gradient Descent is a variant of Gradient Descent that uses random samples from the training data instead of the entire dataset. This makes it faster and more efficient, especially for large datasets.

Back-Propagation

Back-Propagation is the process of calculating the gradient of the loss function with respect to the weights and biases of the Neural Network. It is used to update the weights and biases during training. Back-Propagation works by propagating the error backwards through the layers of the network, adjusting the weights and biases as it goes.

Here's a sample Arduino code for communicating with the Sensirion SHT4x sensor using I2C protocol and transmitting the data in binary ASCII format optimized for LabVIEW:

scssCopy code
#include <Wire.h>

// Define the I2C address of the Sensirion SHT4x sensor
#define SHT4X_ADDR 0x44

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(9600); // Start serial communication with PC
  Wire.begin(); // Start I2C communication
}

void loop() {
  // Send command to measure temperature and humidity
  Wire.beginTransmission(SHT4X_ADDR);
  Wire.write(0x24);
  Wire.write(0x00);
  Wire.endTransmission();

  // Wait for measurement to be completed (duration depends on sensor settings)
  delay(100);

  // Read temperature and humidity values
  Wire.requestFrom(SHT4X_ADDR, 6);
  uint8_t data[6];
  int i = 0;
  while (Wire.available()) {
    data[i] = Wire.read();
    i++;
  }
  
  // Convert data to binary ASCII format optimized for LabVIEW
  int16_t temp_raw = ((data[0] << 8) | data[1]) & 0xFFFC;
  float temperature = -45.0 + 175.0 * (float)temp_raw / 65535.0;
  int16_t humid_raw = ((data[3] << 8) | data[4]) & 0xFFFC;
  float humidity = 100.0 * (float)humid_raw / 65535.0;
  byte buf[8];
  memcpy(buf, &temperature, sizeof(temperature));
  memcpy(buf+4, &humidity, sizeof(humidity));

  // Send data to PC as binary ASCII string
  Serial.write(buf, 8);
}

namespace App\Http\Controllers\Auth;

use App\Http\Controllers\Controller;

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Password;

class ResetPasswordController extends Controller

    /**

     *
     * @param  \Illuminate\Http\Request  $request
     * @return \Illuminate\Http\JsonResponse
     */
    public function reset(Request $request)
    {
        $request->validate([
            'token' => 'required',
            'email' => 'required|email',
            'password' => 'required|min:8|confirmed',

        }
